mainTopic: The end of מגילת תענית, why messengers go out in תשרי and אדר שני, and the length of the two אדרים
overview: This amud opens by finishing the question of whether the minor holidays of מגילת תענית still apply after the חורבן. The גמרא says this is a dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי. It rules that the days were nullified, except for חנוכה and פורים. Next the גמרא returns to the משנה about messengers (שלוחים) who announce ראש חודש, and asks why they go out in תשרי if they already went out in אלול. The answer is that בית דין could make אלול a full month. Then distant communities would keep ראש השנה on the wrong day, but the תשרי messengers save all the festivals that follow. The גמרא then shows that the משנה does not follow רבי, who sends messengers for אדר שני too. It explains that the argument is about how long the added leap-year month is. Finally, several testimonies disagree about whether the two אדרים are full or short, and רב נחמן begins a challenge from the rule that witnesses may break שבת for ניסן. That challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The Sages rule it pure
steps.stepSummary: The tail end of a source quoted in the previous discussion: חכמים rule the item טהור, unlike רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Sages declare it pure.
steps.whatsHappening: These words finish a source the גמרא was quoting on the previous amud, a dispute where רבי מאיר says an item is טמא and חכמים say it is טהור. This closes the earlier discussion and sets up the גמרא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to חכמים, the item still counts as a broken utensil, so it cannot become טמא. The earlier discussion had raised a problem: a new holiday was added to מגילת תענית in רבי מאיר's lifetime, after the חורבן. That seems to show מגילת תענית was not nullified, and the next step answers this problem.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages; the majority opinion of the Rabbis

steps.confusionAlert: This line belongs to the discussion that began on the previous amud. Do not try to read it as the start of a new topic.

phrases.english: And the Sages declare it pure.
phrases.notes: End of a quoted dispute; חכמים treat the utensil as still broken.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Concludes a source cited in the earlier part of the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים rule the item טהור, treating it as a broken utensil.
steps.kashyaTarget: The position that מגילת תענית was nullified after the חורבן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The quoted source places רבי מאיר, and the new holiday instituted through his student רבי יהודה בן שמוע, after the חורבן. That suggests the days of מגילת תענית were still in force.

steps.title: It is a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that whether מגילת תענית was nullified is a dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי, and quotes a ברייתא to show it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a dispute between תנאים, as it was taught: These days written in מגילת תענית are forbidden for fasting whether or not the בית המקדש stands. This is רבי מאיר's view. רבי יוסי says: when the בית המקדש stands they are forbidden, because they are a joy to Israel. When it does not stand they are permitted, because they are a time of mourning for them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the earlier difficulty by saying 'this is a dispute between תנאים.' It quotes a ברייתא where רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי argue about whether the days of מגילת תענית still apply after the חורבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר holds the days always stay in force, so a new holiday could still be added after the חורבן. רבי יוסי holds that without the מקדש the days are a time of mourning, so fasting on them is permitted. The earlier proof only works according to רבי מאיר and does not obligate everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: It is a dispute between תנאים
As it was taught in a ברייתא
The scroll listing minor holidays on which fasting (and sometimes eulogizing) is forbidden

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the status of מגילת תענית depends on whether its joy is tied to the existence of the מקדש.

phrases.english: It is a dispute of Tannaim, as it was taught:
These days that are written in Megillat Ta'anit,
whether at a time when the Temple is standing

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בִּזְמַן שֶׁאֵין בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים —
phrases.english: or at a time when the Temple is not standing —
are forbidden (for fasting); these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
Rabbi Yosei says:
When the Temple is standing — they are forbidden,
because it is a joy for them.
When the Temple is not standing — they are permitted,
because it is mourning for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty raised in the earlier discussion by showing it reflects only one side of a dispute.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The added holiday in רבי מאיר's time proves that everyone holds מגילת תענית was not nullified.
steps.terutzMaskana: That proof fits רבי מאיר only; רבי יוסי holds the days were nullified once the מקדש was gone.

steps.title: Two rulings: nullified and not nullified
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states the halacha in two parts that seem to contradict each other: the days were nullified, and they were not nullified.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the halacha is that they were nullified, and the halacha is that they were not nullified.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final halacha, but it is phrased as two opposite rulings. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This double ruling looks impossible on purpose. The גמרא will show that each ruling applies to a different group of days.

keyTerms.meaning: They were nullified (no longer in force)

phrases.english: And the halacha is: they were nullified,
and the halacha is: they were not nullified.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling on the dispute between רבי מאיר and רבי יוסי.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both rulings are stated as halacha, and they will need to be reconciled.

steps.title: One ruling contradicts the other
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the two halachic rulings contradict each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is difficult: one halacha contradicts the other!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the double ruling it just gave. How can the days be both nullified and not nullified?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taken literally, the two statements cancel each other out. A real answer must divide the cases somehow.

keyTerms.meaning: One halacha contradicts the other halacha

phrases.english: One halacha is difficult against the other halacha!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the internal consistency of the ruling in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The double ruling 'they were nullified / they were not nullified'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two halachos about the same days cannot be opposite.

steps.title: חנוכה and פורים stay; the other days are nullified
steps.stepSummary: The rulings apply to different days: חנוכה and פורים were not nullified, and all the other days of מגילת תענית were nullified.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. Here, it refers to חנוכה and פורים. There, it refers to the rest of the days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by assigning each ruling to a different group of days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Not nullified' refers to חנוכה and פורים, which are also listed in מגילת תענית and still apply today. 'Nullified' refers to every other day in the list. So the halacha follows רבי יוסי for most days, but these two holidays remain.

keyTerms.meaning: Here... there (each statement refers to a different case)

steps.whatToRemember: The halacha is that מגילת תענית is nullified, except for חנוכה and פורים, which remain in force.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is why we do not observe the minor holidays of מגילת תענית today, but we still keep חנוכה and פורים.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
here, regarding Chanukah and Purim,
there, regarding the rest of the days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both rulings refer to all the days of מגילת תענית.
steps.terutzMaskana: חנוכה and פורים were not nullified; the remaining days were.

steps.title: The משנה: messengers in אלול and תשרי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה: שלוחים go out in אלול because of ראש השנה, and in תשרי to set the dates of the festivals.
steps.simpleTranslation: The messengers go out for אלול because of ראש השנה, and for תשרי to establish the correct dates of the festivals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section by quoting the next line of the משנה about the שלוחים. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Messengers are sent in אלול so people know when ראש חודש אלול was declared and can count to ראש השנה. Messengers are also sent in תשרי so people know the right days for סוכות and the other festivals of the month.

keyTerms.meaning: The month of the fall festivals

phrases.english: For Elul, because of Rosh HaShanah,
and for Tishrei, because of setting the festivals correctly.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: returns to the משנה after finishing the מגילת תענית discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שלוחים go out for both אלול and תשרי.

steps.title: Why send messengers again in תשרי?
steps.stepSummary: If the messengers already went out in אלול, why do they need to go out again in תשרי?
steps.simpleTranslation: Since they already went out for אלול, why do they need to go out for תשרי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. Once people know when אלול began, they should already know when תשרי begins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The assumption is that אלול always has 29 days, so ראש חודש תשרי is always the 30th day after ראש חודש אלול. If so, the אלול messengers already give people everything they need, and the תשרי trip seems unnecessary. The answer comes next.

phrases.english: Since they already went out for Elul,
why do they need to go out for Tishrei?

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיוָן דְּנָפְקִי לְהוּ אַאֱלוּל, אַתִּשְׁרִי לְמָה לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the second set of messengers listed in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that שלוחים also go out for תשרי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ראש חודש תשרי can be calculated from ראש חודש אלול, so a second announcement seems pointless.

steps.title: Maybe בית דין added a day to אלול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a reason for the תשרי messengers: בית דין might have made אלול a full 30-day month.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say: perhaps they made אלול a full month by adding a day,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering the question from step 7. It suggests that the messengers of תשרי are needed because אלול might have been lengthened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The messengers of אלול tell people when ראש חודש אלול was. People far away then count 30 days to reach ראש השנה, assuming אלול has only 29 days. If בית דין added a day to אלול, that count would be wrong, so a second set of messengers in תשרי would be needed.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say (introduces a suggested idea)
They made it full (added a day to the month)

phrases.english: And if you say
perhaps they added a day to Elul (made it a full month),
phrases.notes: If אלול has 30 days, ראש השנה falls on the 31st day after ראש חודש אלול, not the 30th.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to the question of step 7
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a case where the אלול messengers are not enough
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The messengers of אלול are enough to fix every date in תשרי
steps.terutzMaskana: If אלול might be full, the dates of תשרי are uncertain and need a second announcement

steps.title: But אלול has not been full since the days of עזרא
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion is challenged with רב's statement that אלול has never been made full since עזרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי חיננא בר כהנא say in the name of רב: from the days of עזרא onward, we have never found a full אלול!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the suggestion it just made. If אלול is never lengthened, the תשרי messengers still seem unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רב, אלול has always had 29 days since the time of עזרא. In that case ראש השנה is always exactly 30 days after ראש חודש אלול, and everyone can work out the festivals of תשרי by themselves. So the reason given in step 8 seems to fall away.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't [so-and-so] say? (introduces a contradicting source)
From the days of עזרא and onward

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי חִינָּנָא בַּר כָּהֲנָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Ḥinnana bar Kahana say that Rav said:
From the days of Ezra and onward
we have not found Elul to be full!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי חִינָּנָא בַּר כָּהֲנָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that אלול might be made full
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An authoritative report says אלול was never full, so the case behind the תשרי messengers never happens

steps.title: It never happened only because it was never needed
steps.stepSummary: רב's statement only reports past practice. If a full אלול were ever needed, they would add the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'We have not found' means it was not needed. But if it were needed, we would add the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 9 by explaining what רב really meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב did not say it is forbidden to make אלול full. He only reported that it never happened, because there was never a reason to do it. Since it is still possible, the תשרי messengers are still needed, and the answer from step 8 stands.

keyTerms.meaning: We add a day to it (make it full)

steps.confusionAlert: 'We have not found' is not a rule that says 'we may not.' It describes what happened in practice, not what is allowed.

phrases.english: 'We have not found' means that it was not necessary;
but if it were necessary, we would add a day to it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 9 and restores the answer of step 8
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the source: a report of practice, not a prohibition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב meant that אלול can never be full
steps.terutzMaskana: אלול can be full when needed, so the תשרי messengers are still necessary

steps.title: But then ראש השנה would be ruined
steps.stepSummary: If בית דין adds a day to אלול, distant communities will keep ראש השנה on the wrong day.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then ראש השנה would be ruined!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with the idea of a full אלול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Distant communities count 30 days from ראש חודש אלול and keep ראש השנה on that day. If אלול was made full, the real ראש השנה is one day later. The messengers of תשרי cannot reach them in time, so they will have kept ראש השנה on the wrong day. How could בית דין allow that?

keyTerms.meaning: The New Year festival on the first of תשרי

phrases.english: But then Rosh HaShana will be ruined!
phrases.notes: Because distant communities will celebrate it on the 30th day after ראש חודש אלול instead of the 31st.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the conclusion of step 10 that אלול may be made full
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that בית דין would make אלול full when needed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A full אלול means far-away people keep ראש השנה on the wrong day, which seems unacceptable

steps.title: Better to lose ראש השנה than all the festivals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that ראש השנה may be ruined. It is better than ruining all the later festivals of תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is better that ראש השנה be ruined, and not all the festivals be ruined.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge of step 11. Yes, ראש השנה may be lost, but that is the lesser loss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Losing ראש השנה is a loss of one festival. The messengers of תשרי make sure that יום כיפור, סוכות, and שמיני עצרת are kept on the correct days. So when needed, בית דין accepts the smaller loss in order to protect the larger one.

keyTerms.meaning: The festivals (here: יום כיפור, סוכות, שמיני עצרת)

steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the whole purpose of the תשרי messengers. They do not save ראש השנה, but they save all the festivals after it.

phrases.english: Better that Rosh HaShana be ruined
and that all the Festivals not be ruined.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11
steps.terutzResolutionType: Accepting the problem as the lesser of two losses
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Ruining ראש השנה is too much, so אלול could never be made full
steps.terutzMaskana: When needed, losing ראש השנה is acceptable in order to protect all the later festivals

steps.title: The wording of the משנה supports this
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the messengers go out in תשרי for the festivals, not for ראש השנה. This fits the explanation, and the גמרא concludes it is correct.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also precise, because the משנה teaches: in תשרי, for setting the festivals. Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support from the exact words of the משנה and then closes the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives the reason for the תשרי messengers as 'תקנת המועדות', the festivals. It does not mention ראש השנה. That matches the idea that ראש השנה may already be lost, and the messengers come to protect the festivals that follow. 'שמע מינה' confirms that this reading is correct.

keyTerms.meaning: The wording is also precise (supports this)
Setting the festivals in proper order

steps.whatToRemember: The messengers of תשרי exist because אלול could be made full. In that case ראש השנה may be lost for distant communities, but the messengers save יום כיפור, סוכות, and שמיני עצרת. The משנה's words 'תקנת המועדות' confirm this.

phrases.english: The language is also precise, as it teaches:
'In Tishrei, due to the setting of the Festivals,'
phrases.notes: The משנה mentions the festivals, not ראש השנה.

phrases.english: Conclude from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 12 from the wording of the משנה quoted in step 6
steps.raayaObject: That the תשרי messengers protect the later festivals even if ראש השנה is lost
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's phrase 'מפני תקנת המועדות', which mentions the festivals and not ראש השנה
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The תשרי messengers are needed in case אלול was made full, and they protect the festivals that come after ראש השנה.

steps.title: The משנה does not mention אדר שני
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the end of the משנה (כסלו for חנוכה, אדר for פורים). It notes that the משנה never says messengers also go out for אדר שני in a leap year, so the משנה must not follow רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says messengers go out in כסלו because of חנוכה and in אדר because of פורים. But it does not say: 'If the year was a leap year, they also go out in אדר שני because of פורים.' So our משנה does not follow רבי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the last part of the משנה's list and points out something missing: there is no mention of a leap year. From that silence, it concludes that the משנה does not agree with רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a leap year there are two months of אדר, and פורים falls in the second one. If the author of the משנה thought messengers were needed for אדר שני, he should have said so. Because he left it out, the גמרא infers that this author disagrees with רבי, whose view is quoted in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The month of כסלו, when חנוכה falls
The year was made a leap year (an extra month was added)
The second אדר, added in a leap year
It does not teach (the text leaves this out)
Our משנה does not follow רבי

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'רבי' means רבי יהודה הנשיא, the editor of the משנה. The גמרא is saying that this particular unnamed משנה does not match his personal opinion.

phrases.english: And in Kislev, because of Chanukah,
and in Adar, because of Purim.
But 'if the year was made a leap year'

phrases.aramaic: יוֹצְאִין אַף עַל אֲדָר שֵׁנִי מִפְּנֵי הַפּוּרִים —
phrases.english: 'they go out also in the second Adar because of Purim'
it does not teach.
phrases.notes: The משנה is silent about a leap year.

phrases.english: Our Mishnah is not in line with Rebbi.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִילּוּ נִתְעַבְּרָה הַשָּׁנָה יוֹצְאִין אַף עַל אֲדָר שֵׁנִי מִפְּנֵי הַפּוּרִים לָא קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the discussion of תשרי to the last months listed in the משנה, כסלו and אדר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because the משנה is silent about אדר שני, it does not follow רבי.

steps.title: רבי's view: messengers also go out for אדר שני
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי holds that in a leap year messengers also go out in אדר שני for פורים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught in a ברייתא: רבי says, if the year was made a leap year, the messengers also go out in אדר שני because of פורים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that records רבי's opinion. This proves that רבי holds the view the משנה left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא states in so many words what the משנה omitted. That confirms the inference from step 14: the author of the משנה and רבי disagree about sending messengers for אדר שני.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: As it was taught: Rebbi says:
If the year was made a leap year,

phrases.aramaic: יוֹצְאִין אַף עַל אֲדָר הַשֵּׁנִי מִפְּנֵי הַפּוּרִים.
phrases.english: they go out also in the second Adar, because of Purim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the claim made in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the משנה does not follow רבי
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא quoting רבי: in a leap year, messengers also go out in אדר שני

steps.title: Suggestion: they disagree whether the מצוות of אדר work in אדר ראשון
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the argument depends on whether the מצוות of אדר שני also work if done in אדר ראשון.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is what they argue about? One Sage holds that all the מצוות done in the second אדר also work in the first. The other Sage holds that all the מצוות done in the second אדר do not work in the first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible reason for the argument between the משנה and רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The author of the משנה might hold that the מצוות of פורים also count if done in אדר ראשון. Then the messengers sent for the first אדר are enough, and none are needed for the second. רבי might hold that they must be done in אדר שני, so he needs messengers for that month too.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a suggestion the גמרא may later reject)
The מצוות practiced in the second אדר (such as פורים)
They also apply, or work, in the first אדר

steps.confusionAlert: The word לימא usually means the suggestion is about to be rejected. Do not treat this as the final answer.

phrases.english: Shall we say they argue about this:
that one Sage holds:
all the מצוות practiced in the second (Adar)
also apply in the first,
and the other Sage holds:
all the מצוות practiced in the second (Adar)
do not apply in the first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to explain the reason behind the argument found in steps 14-15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Proposed: the argument depends on whether the מצוות of אדר work if done in אדר ראשון.

steps.title: Rejection: everyone agrees, and they argue about the leap-year month
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Everyone agrees the מצוות of אדר שני do not work in אדר ראשון. The real argument is about the extra leap-year month.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees that the מצוות practiced in the second אדר do not work in the first. Here they argue about the leap-year addition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back the suggestion and moves the argument to a different question: how long the added month is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree that פורים belongs in אדר שני. So the question is only whether people can figure out its date on their own. That depends on whether the added month has a fixed length, which the next step shows.

keyTerms.meaning: Making the year a leap year (the added month)

phrases.english: No, everyone agrees that
the מצוות practiced in the second (Adar)
do not apply in the first,
and here they argue about the leap-year addition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of step 16 and offers another explanation.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole idea that the argument is about the מצוות of אדר ראשון
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: There is no need to make the two sides argue about that, since both can agree and still disagree about the length of the added month.

steps.title: Source: is the added month thirty days or just 'a month'?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records the argument. The תנא קמא says the added month is thirty days. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says it is 'a month.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: How long is the leap-year addition? Thirty days. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: a month.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that there really is an argument about the length of the added month.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the added month is always thirty days, people can count to אדר שני themselves, so no messengers are needed. That fits the משנה. If it is just 'a month,' its length is unknown, so messengers are needed. That fits רבי, who follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: The תנא who says the addition is 'a month'

steps.whyThisMatters: This ties the question of sending messengers to a simple practical issue: can people work out the date on their own?

phrases.english: As it was taught: How much is the leap-year addition?
Thirty days.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: חֹדֶשׁ.
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: A month.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for the argument named in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That there is an argument about the length of the added month
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: the תנא קמא says thirty days, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says a month

steps.title: Challenge: a month is also a known length
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why thirty days is easier to know than 'a month.' A plain month is twenty-nine days, so people would know that too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is thirty days different, because people know it? They also know 'a month'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the explanation from step 17. 'A month' also seems to be a known length, so why would it need messengers?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The explanation needs רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's 'month' to be of unknown length. But 'a month' normally means twenty-nine days, which is also fixed. If so, people could count by themselves under both views, and the reason for the argument falls apart.

phrases.english: What is different about thirty, that they know it?
A month they also know!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the explanation of steps 17-18.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'a month' leaves the date unknown and so requires messengers
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A month also has a known length (twenty-nine days), so people could count on their own.

steps.title: רב פפא: 'a month' can be either twenty-nine or thirty
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that according to the view of 'a month,' the court may choose to add twenty-nine days or thirty. So people cannot know, and messengers are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The one who says 'a month' means that if the court wants, it adds a month of twenty-nine days, and if it wants, it adds thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the challenge by showing that 'a month' does not have a fixed length.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since בית דין can choose twenty-nine or thirty days, people far away cannot work out when אדר שני begins. Therefore רבי, following רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, needs messengers for אדר שני. The משנה, holding a fixed thirty days, does not.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who gives the answer

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree פורים is in אדר שני. The משנה sends no messengers for אדר שני because the added month is a fixed thirty days. רבי sends them because, following רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, בית דין may add twenty-nine or thirty days, so people cannot know the date.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
The one who says 'a month' means:
if (the court) wants, a month (of twenty-nine days),
if it wants, thirty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: מַאן דְּאָמַר חֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'A month' means a fixed twenty-nine days, so people would know the date.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'A month' means בית דין may add either twenty-nine or thirty days, so the date is unknown and messengers are needed.

steps.title: Both months of אדר are sanctified on their thirtieth day
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי testifies in the name of the holy community of ירושלים that both months of אדר are sanctified on the day that could have made them full, which is day thirty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי testified in the name of the holy community of ירושלים about the two months of אדר: the new month after each of them is sanctified on day thirty, the day that would otherwise have been added to make the month full.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new testimony about how long the two אדרים are in a leap year.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A month is either 29 days (short) or 30 days (full). If the next ראש חודש is declared on day thirty, the old month stopped after 29 days. So this testimony means both אדרים are always short.

keyTerms.meaning: testified (a formal report of an accepted ruling or practice)
the holy community of ירושלים, a respected group of sages
the two months of אדר in a leap year
the day that would be added to make a month full (day thirty)

steps.confusionAlert: 'ביום עיבוריהן' does NOT mean the months are made full. It means ראש חודש is declared on the day that COULD have made them full. So the months end up short.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi testified
in the name of the holy community of Jerusalem
about the two months of Adar
that they are sanctified on the day of their possible extension (day thirty)
phrases.notes: The next month begins on day 30, so each אדר has only 29 days.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵעִיד רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי מִשּׁוּם קְהָלָא קַדִּישָׁא דִּירוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the length of the added month to a testimony about the length of both אדרים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both אדרים are sanctified on day thirty, so both are 29-day (short) months.

steps.title: Does this mean the אדרים are only ever short?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא draws the implication: the court makes the אדרים short and never full.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that to say that we make them short, and we do not make them full?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pulls out what the testimony implies and sets up the next step, which explains who the testimony is arguing against.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'sanctified on day thirty' is a fixed rule, so there is no choice to make them full. The גמרא spells this out to ask what the testimony is coming to exclude.

keyTerms.meaning: is that to say / this implies

phrases.english: Is that to say that we make them short,
but we do not make them full?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the implication from רבי יהושע בן לוי's testimony.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the testimony really saying the אדרים can never be full, and if so, whom does it exclude?

steps.title: It excludes the view that the court may choose
steps.stepSummary: Yes: the testimony comes to reject רב נחמן בר חסדא's teaching. He quoted רבי סימאי in the name of חגי, זכריה and מלאכי that the court may make the two אדרים full, short, or one of each.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, it comes to exclude what רב נחמן בר חסדא taught: רבי סימאי testified in the name of חגי, זכריה and מלאכי about the two אדרים, that if the court wants to make both full, they may; both short, they may; one full and one short, they may. And this is how they would act in the גולה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יהושע בן לוי is arguing against a different testimony that gives the court free choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are now two opposite testimonies. רבי יהושע בן לוי says the אדרים are always short. רבי סימאי, quoting the prophets, says the court may decide any combination, and that this was the practice in the גולה.

keyTerms.meaning: the last three prophets, members of the early great court

phrases.aramaic: לְאַפּוֹקֵי מִדְּדָרֵשׁ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר חִסְדָּא.
phrases.english: This is to exclude what Rav Naḥman bar Ḥisda taught.
Rabbi Simai testified
in the name of Haggai, Zechariah, and Malachi
about the two months of Adar,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם רָצוּ לַעֲשׂוֹתָן שְׁנֵיהֶן מְלֵאִין — עוֹשִׂין,
phrases.english: that if they want to make them both full, they may do so;
both short, they may do so;
one full and one short, they may do so;
and this is how they would act in the Diaspora.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאַפּוֹקֵי מִדְּדָרֵשׁ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה by naming the opposing view that the testimony rejects.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, the אדרים are always short. This rejects רבי סימאי's testimony that the court may choose any combination.

steps.title: רב's practice: one full and one short
steps.stepSummary: In the name of רב they said: the two אדרים are always treated as one full and one short, unless you know that ראש חודש was fixed at its usual time.
steps.simpleTranslation: And in the name of our teacher (רב) they said: always treat them as one full and one short, unless you find out that ראש חודש was set at its proper time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another opinion, from רב, about how to count the two אדרים in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב gives a default rule for people who do not know what the court decided: count one אדר as full and one as short. If you learn that ראש חודש was set on time, meaning the first אדר was also short, you follow that instead.

keyTerms.meaning: until it becomes known to you

phrases.english: And in the name of our teacher (Rav) they said:
always one full and one short,
unless it becomes known to you
that the New Moon was fixed at its proper time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רב נחמן בר חסדא's teaching with רב's default practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By default, count the two אדרים as one full and one short, unless you learn that ראש חודש was set on time.

steps.title: The אדר next to ניסן is always short
steps.stepSummary: A ruling was sent from ארץ ישראל to מר עוקבא: the אדר right before ניסן is always short.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent a message to מר עוקבא: the אדר that is next to ניסן is always short.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ruling sent to בבל: the אדר right before ניסן always has 29 days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This rule speaks only about the אדר next to ניסן, the regular אדר or אדר שני. It says nothing fixed about אדר ראשון, so that month could sometimes be full.

keyTerms.meaning: they sent to him (a ruling sent from ארץ ישראל)
the one right next to (before) ניסן

phrases.english: They sent to Mar Ukva:
The Adar adjacent to Nisan is always short.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another ruling about the length of אדר, limited to the אדר before ניסן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The אדר directly before ניסן is always 29 days.

steps.title: רב נחמן challenges from breaking שבת for ניסן
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes the משנה that witnesses may break שבת to report the new moon for ניסן and תשרי. That makes sense only if the אדר before ניסן is sometimes full and sometimes short.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן objected: for two months witnesses may break שבת, for ניסן and for תשרי. Granted, if you say the אדר is sometimes full and sometimes short, that is why they break שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן starts a challenge against the ruling that the אדר before ניסן is always short. The second half of the challenge comes in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Witnesses break שבת only when their testimony can change something. If אדר can be 29 or 30 days, the witnesses decide when ניסן starts, so breaking שבת is justified. The implied attack: if אדר is always short, ניסן starts on a known day anyway, so why break שבת?

keyTerms.meaning: raises an objection (from an earlier source)
the months with major holidays (פסח; ראש השנה, יום כיפור, סוכות)
granted, if you say (sets up a contrast)

steps.whyThisMatters: It tests whether a fixed calendar rule fits the משנה's rule that witnesses may break שבת. If the length of אדר is fixed, their testimony seems useless.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman raised an objection:

phrases.aramaic: עַל שְׁנֵי חֳדָשִׁים מְחַלְּלִין אֶת הַשַּׁבָּת —
phrases.english: For two months they may desecrate Shabbat:
for Nisan and for Tishrei.
Granted, if you say
that it is sometimes full and sometimes short,
because of that we desecrate Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling sent to מר עוקבא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that the אדר next to ניסן is always short.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה lets witnesses break שבת for ניסן. That only makes sense if their testimony decides whether אדר is 29 or 30 days. If אדר is always short, there is no reason to break שבת.
